title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 76A (Punishment for contravention of section 73 or 76)

content.overview: Section 76A prescribes company and officer penalties, and a fine on the company of not less than one crore rupees, for contravention of s. 73 or s. 76, with a higher consequence where fraud is proved.
content.glance: Section 76A prescribes company and officer penalties, and a fine on the company of not less than one crore rupees, for contravention of s. 73 or s. 76, with a higher consequence where fraud is proved.
content.study: The section is the dedicated sanction for the deposit chapter. The company is liable to a fine of at least one crore rupees and up to ten crore rupees. Every officer in default is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years or a fine of at least twenty-five lakh rupees and up to two crore rupees, or both. If the contravention is proved to be fraudulent, liability is attracted under s. 447. The penalty does not replace the duty to repay. Section 76A was inserted by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015.

distinctions: Section 76A is the deposit-chapter penalty. Section 447 is the general fraud offence and applies on proof of fraud.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is repayment the only consequence of an illegal deposit?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Section 76A adds fine and possible imprisonment, and s. 447 applies if fraud is proved.
